review: Eligibility instants round down so comparison cannot select a persisted deadline early. Empty polls exercise the real PostgreSQL query codec with a fixed nanosecond clock.
Successful publication persists a microsecond-aligned completion instant while the injected application clock retains its original nanoseconds.
Retry delay is added to the original completion sample before rounding up. Tests cover whole and fractional microseconds, one-nanosecond delay, aligned deadlines and second rollover.
Each retry test reloads the committed record, rejects polling before the exact original and stored deadlines, then accepts at the stored deadline with the same publication ID and next attempt.
Cancellation rolls back publication changes and leaves the database/row/capacity reusable. Existing post-commit observation, failure classification and locking tests remain green.

The existing job outbox rollback/lost-response test now forces a nanosecond clock and still requires a single accepted queue identity after reconciliation. Existing Redis integration and public consumer cases also pass.

Both strict time.Time and temporal.DateTime SQL codecs still reject explicit sub-microsecond caller values. Generic temporal construction preserves the same nanoseconds; clock and codec implementations are unchanged.

The change adds no API, dependency, schema migration, generated setting or alternate timestamp subsystem. Publisher timing policy remains at its SQL boundary; framework model timestamps keep their existing owner.

The full gate includes vet, package/consumer tests, real editor and client checks, deterministic generation checks, documentation checks and release-helper tests. The phase=failure exit=7 stdout item is an intentional passing runner unit test; make and the Python suite both pass.
